A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GIT-BO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–C report original optimization benchmarks and ablations, including outcomes across 20 independent trials.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–D and G report original benchmark, ablation, intrinsic-dimension recovery, and surrogate accuracy/runtime results.

M1.justification: The frozen TabPFN surrogate, gradient diagnostic matrix, eigenspace search, and centroid back-projection remain. v3 adds quantile-UCB and variance-threshold rank-selection variants. Its default acquisition is described as UCB instead of TS, but both versions describe 512 posterior draws, so the naming change alone does not establish a wholly different default implementation.

E1.justification: v3 removes LassoSyntheticMedium/High, LassoDNA, and SVM, and adds 102D Walker policy search, changing the main suite from 63 to 60 variants. Renamed power-system and car benchmarks are retained. Appendix C additionally evaluates low-intrinsic-dimensional embeddings of Branin, Ackley, and Levy as distinct subspace-recovery scenarios.

E2.justification: HESBO and ALEBO, each evaluated at embedding dimensions 10 and 20 in v1, are replaced by BAxUS and Vanilla BO. v3 specifies SAASBO-MAP from Xu et al., whereas v1 identifies a BoTorch tutorial implementation. Additional comparisons include GI-equipped EI and an untuned GP(EI)+GI control.

E3.justification: The main evaluation changes from 100 iterations for all methods and 200 for selected methods to 500 for all; v3 also states a 10,000-second trial limit. The default subspace rank changes from 15 to 10. The acquisition ablation replaces 100D synthetic instances with 500D instances, while the shared 200-point LHS initialization remains.

E4.justification: The existing GI/no-GI and fixed-rank analyses are expanded with adaptive variance-based rank selection, quantile-versus-sampling UCB and exploration-factor sweeps, and alternative subspace sampling strategies. v3 also adds intrinsic-dimension recovery experiments and a stock-versus-differentiable TabPFN accuracy/runtime analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 20 independently seeded trials, median convergence curves with 95% confidence intervals, and Friedman/Wilcoxon tests with Holm correction. However, v3 removes the dedicated trial-distribution violin plots and variance-ranking reports in v1 Figures 9, 11, and 12. No increase in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: Figure 2 reports GIT-BO's overall rank as 1.97 in v1 and 1.92 in v3 under different suites, baselines, and budgets; this is not a same-setting improvement. v3 newly reports BAxUS leading the synthetic subset, expanded parameter-sweep results, intrinsic-dimension recovery, and the surrogate accuracy/runtime tradeoff. Results for removed benchmarks and variance analyses disappear.

T1.justification: v1 presents method equations and cites dimension-reduction theory without formal guarantees. v3 Appendix A introduces noise, RKHS, and TabPFN-approximation assumptions; confidence and information-gain bounds; sampling/quantile-UCB equivalence claims; a regret theorem; and a convergence corollary. These are substantial new theoretical claims, although complete supporting proofs are not supplied.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains retraining-free high-dimensional BO using a foundation model and gradient-informed subspaces. v3's abstract shifts emphasis from consistently outperforming GP methods to a performance–runtime tradeoff, explicitly qualifies model-capacity and memory limits, and updates the claimed empirical scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations involving persistent PFN bias, synthetic-versus-engineering generalization, and surrogate gradient quality as an explanation for subspace recovery. It discusses the single-estimator implementation's accuracy tradeoff and acknowledges inference costs relative to simple GPs. The GPU requirement, 500D limit, and several difficult benchmark families were already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses single-estimator TabPFN inference, fixed standardization, and omitted ensemble/preprocessing operations; v1 only describes a differentiable wrapper, so an implementation change is not established. Baseline and Walker implementation provenance is expanded. The anonymous GIT-BO URL disappears, while a release-upon-acceptance statement conflicts with a retained reference to a supplied code zip, leaving actual availability unresolved.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially rebuilt around additive BO, classical active and likelihood-informed subspaces, learned latent representations, and PFN limitations. Added works include Constantine et al., Nagler, Ye et al., and Reuter et al. This replaces much of v1's LLM-gradient and gradient-enhanced GP motivation with a different account of why frozen TFMs need structural guidance.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, method exposition, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Background and method material gain numbered subsections, the conclusion becomes separate, and appendices are reorganized with a contents page. References move before the appendices, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, ranking panels are reorganized, and extensive regret-versus-runtime displays are added. Benchmark curves are regrouped with revised legends and logarithmic axes, while violin and variance-ranking figures disappear. Rank summaries gain tables, the penalty table is reformatted, and new ablation, recovery, and implementation figures substantially alter the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Matched 500-iteration budgets, per-problem runtime curves, and expanded controls strengthen v3's empirical evaluation. However, Appendix A adds guarantees without complete supporting proofs, and Appendix B.1 claims acquisition-independent success despite Figure 6 showing EI+GI performing poorly on the synthetic tasks. These empirical gains coexist with new rigor and interpretation problems, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
